purpose: Establish signed pair preconditions from actual eight-block inputs, actual evaluations and verified products, rather than requiring numeric output properties from an unverified caller.
input_domain: Equal-length full-u64 limb slices a and b; 7*k <= length <= 8*k, including k=0 and an empty eighth block; eight bounded nonnegative weights under the existing evaluation contract; caller-owned disjoint outputs and scratch.
output_meaning: Even and odd diagonal weighted sums of the independent input-block product. The ghost-only convolution identity groups the same 64 input products into fifteen independently defined coefficients under an explicit multiplicative-weight premise.
execution: Four existing signed evaluations, two existing verified full products, one simultaneous sum/difference pass, and two exact halvings. No new allocator, matrix interpolation, FFI, intrinsic or trusted proof escape.
local_workspace: Two m-word evaluation buffers followed by at least 12*m child scratch words; m=k+1. Two separate outputs each contain 2*m words. This is a local 14*m scratch interface, not a proof of the whole Toom8 12*n/10*n schedule.
local_work: 2*T_existing_full(m)+O(k), with existing forced Toom4 children in this composition prototype. A complete recursive Toom8 kernel must replace those child calls with its own decreasing recursion and establish the complete recurrence separately.
derived_obligations: Positive evaluation is below 2^22*B^k and dominates the magnitude of negative evaluation.
Point products have nonnegative even and odd decompositions, imply positive-product >= abs(negative-product), and have matching parity.
The sum of product magnitudes fits the actual 2*(k+1) output words.
remaining: Fresh full immutable feature gate and independent review
Dyadic weight product identities and coefficient-level caller bridge
Actual endpoint removal/scaling and Newton preconditions
Fifteen-point recursion, recomposition and complete scratch lifetime proof
Performance acceptance under a separately approved frozen experiment
code_generation_boundary: A private non-inlined normalization helper retains the complete existing half_pair contract; this permits LLVM to remove element bounds guards in the composed path. The constant call cost has not been timed.
